'''Stefan Dietrich Güttel''' (born 27 November 1981) is a German [[Numerical analysis|numerical analyst]]. He is Professor of [[Applied Mathematics]] in the [[Department of Mathematics, University of Manchester|Department of Mathematics]] at the [[University of Manchester]].

Güttel was born in [[Dresden]], and was educated at the [[Freiberg University of Mining and Technology]], from which he gained his MSc in Applied Mathematics (2006) and PhD in Applied Mathematics (2010). His PhD thesis ''Rational Krylov Methods for Operator Functions'' was supervised by [[Michael Eiermann]].<ref name="mathgene">{{MathGenealogy|id=176258}}</ref> He worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the [[University of Geneva]] (2010–2011) and the [[University of Oxford]] (2011–2012). In 2012 he was appointed lecturer in mathematics at the University of Manchester, and later promoted to Senior Lecturer and Reader. In 2021 he was promoted to Professor of Applied Mathematics.<ref name="cv">{{Cite web|url=https://personalpages.manchester.ac.uk/staff/stefan.guettel/guettel_webcv.pdf|title=Web CV of Stefan Güttel|website=personalpages.manchester.ac.uk|access-date=2026-04-18}}</ref>

Güttel is best known for his work on numerical algorithms for large-scale problems arising with differential equations and in data science, in particular [[Krylov subspace]] methods. He worked with companies such as [[Intel]], [[Schlumberger]], and [[Arup Group|Arup]].

Since 2018 Güttel is a Fellow of the [[Alan Turing Institute]],<ref>[https://www.turing.ac.uk/people/researchers/stefan-guttel Stefan Güttel's Turing Fellow page]</ref> the United Kingdom's national institute for data science and artificial intelligence. In 2018 he received a Teaching Excellence Award of the University of Manchester. In 2021 he was awarded the [[James H. Wilkinson Prize in Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing]] by the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) for ''his contributions to the analysis, implementation, and application of rational and block Krylov methods'' (laudatio),<ref>[https://www.manchester.ac.uk/discover/news/dr-stefan-guettel-awarded-2021-siam-james-h-wilkinson-prize/ Dr Stefan Güttel awarded 2021 SIAM James H Wilkinson Prize], University of Manchester, 11 Dezember 2020</ref> which have become popular for the efficient numerical solution of large eigenvalue problems, matrix equations, and in model order reduction. In 2023 he received the [[ILAS Taussky–Todd Prize|Taussky–Todd Prize]] of the [[International Linear Algebra Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ilasic.org/taussky-todd-lecturers/|title=ILAS Taussky–Todd Prize Recipients|website=International Linear Algebra Society|date=31 December 2020}}</ref> In 2026 he was elected a SIAM Fellow.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/publications/siam-news/articles/siam-announces-2026-class-of-fellows/|title=SIAM Announces 2026 Class of Fellows|website=Society of Industrial and Applied Mathematics|date=18 April 2026}}</ref>

Güttel has served as the elected Secretary and Treasurer of the UK and Republic of Ireland section of SIAM (2016–2018) and is a member of SIAM's membership committee (since 2020). He served on the editorial boards of the [[SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing]] (2015–2021) and [[Electronic Transactions on Numerical Analysis]] (since 2020).<ref name="cv"/>
